formula.cost_per_task: p / q, where q is successful completed tasks per hour at fixed work, quality and latency/service-level requirements
formula.inequality_proof: p_Intel / q_Intel <= p_rival / q_rival iff q_Intel / q_rival >= p_Intel / p_rival, for positive prices and throughput
formula.fixed_batch_equivalent: If identical fixed work completes in time t, p_Intel * t_Intel <= p_rival * t_rival iff t_Intel/t_rival <= p_rival/p_Intel

interpretive_limits: Equal billed OCPUs and advertised vCPUs do not imply equal physical cores, instructions, throughput, or customer value.
The Intel-versus-AMD threshold is 2.8942% greater successful throughput, not a measured performance result. Its fixed-work runtime equivalent is 2.8128% less time, not 2.8942% less time.

The 32 GB basket has 8 GB per OCPU. Ranking changes with memory configuration: Intel is cheaper than AMD below 3.1667 GB per OCPU and cheaper than Ampere below 2.3667 GB per OCPU at equal billed OCPU count, before workload performance.
Storage, egress, paid operating-system licenses, support, tax and discounts are excluded. Adding other costs can alter the break-even ratio; the 2.89% threshold is for the defined CPU+memory basket.
Retail CPU and memory line-item allocation does not reveal processor transaction prices, cloud hardware bill of materials, Intel ASP, margins or price elasticity.
Three offerings from one provider are a bounded descriptive comparison; not a representative customer sample or a market-share estimate.
No paid cloud instance, original workload benchmark, original customer interview, or undisclosed procurement evidence was used.

reject_as_matched_evidence.reason: X12 is compared with older Intel X9, not AMD E6 Ax; bare-metal and VM gains are different comparisons.
E6 Ax improvement is versus E6 Standard; X12 improvement is versus X9. Baselines differ and reported gains cannot be divided to infer an Intel-versus-AMD ratio.
Author explicitly states he has not run a side-by-side X12-versus-E6 test for this harness runtime. Article provides no paired throughput dataset usable here.

matched_benchmark_search.conclusion: Keep both observed throughput and observed cost/task null. The search establishes an evidence gap in reviewed material, not proof that no benchmark exists anywhere.

approved_exhibit_language: At Oracle’s listed 4-OCPU/32-GB configuration, Intel X12 Ax costs $0.4124 per hour in CPU and memory versus $0.4008 for AMD E6 Ax. Intel would need 2.89% more successful tasks per hour to match that rental cost per task. This is a calculated break-even, not measured workload performance.
approved_table_note: All three configurations advertise 8 vCPUs; physical cores are 4 Intel, 4 AMD and 8 Ampere. CPU+memory list prices exclude other cloud charges.
